qualification: local A05.4 exact-recovery-mask acceptance; not hardware, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidate.description: Tier-one publishes per-instruction live-in and cumulative-dirty GPR masks derived from optimized IR. Opaque helpers remain all-register conservative.
candidate.hostControlBoundary: Memory-capable generated blocks restore incoming FP/LR from append-only context words rather than generated stack storage.
candidate.machineCodeEffectOfMasks: The mask values are side-table metadata and do not alter compiled block machineWords.

verification.focused: 80 tests in the metadata and Tier-one suites passed.
verification.deterministicAggregate: 1,546 tests in 179 suites passed with test parallelism disabled; the environment-driven pinned boot test skipped because its variables were absent, then the same pinned inputs were executed explicitly twice.
parallelHarnessObservations: One parallel aggregate failed only concurrentPendingWorkRequestStopsBeforeTheFirstNativeInstruction; the test passed immediately in isolation.
A second parallel aggregate passed that test and failed only lockedNativeCompareExchangeSharesGateAcrossTranslatedBusViews; that test passed immediately in isolation.
The failures affected distinct internally concurrent timing tests and did not occur in the exact-mask or recovery suites.

disposition.reason: Both independent runs crossed the former approximate 208.8-second failure window, four aggregate code-cache wraps, all seven authenticated workloads, and clean ACPI poweroff without an invalid generated return.
disposition.remainingA05_4Work: Baseline inline-TLB page faults still use whole-block rollback and interpreter replay; their production-safe precise-prefix recovery remains open.

limitations: Two passing local runs are a bounded reliability check, not proof of the former overwrite mechanism.
Parallel aggregate scheduling remains noisy for two unrelated internally concurrent tests; both pass in isolation and the full deterministic aggregate passes.
This evidence does not satisfy the greater-than-95-percent dispatcher gate or G1-G5.
